newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi Aramco to end Shaybah oilfield in mid-98.
newsitem.headline: Saudi Aramco to end Shaybah oilfield in mid-98.

text.p: State-owned oil firm Saudi Aramco said on Wednesday major work to develop its Shaybah oilfield in the remote Empty Quarter will come on stream by mid-1998, a year ahead of previous plans.

"Inshallah (Godwilling), workers in Aramco are keen to complete the project by mid-1998...where as the previous schedule for completion was mid-1999," Aramco chief Abdullah Saleh Juma told Oil Minister Ali bin Ibrahim al-Nuaimi.
His remarks, carried by the Saudi state-run news agency, were made during a tour of the multi-million dollar project in the barren desert by Nuaimi. The agency gave no further details.
Aramco signed major contracts for the project in July, oil industry sources in Saudi said.
The fast-track award of these contracts reflected Aramco's desire to bring initial output from the 500,000 barrels per day (bpd) capacity oilfield on stream as early as the end of 1998, they said.
Firms only submitted their bids to carry out the estimated $1.7 billion worth of work six weeks earlier.

Shaybah is Aramco's main upstream project and is being developed to maintain the kingdom's capacity to produce 10 million bpd and retain its position as the world's biggest oil producer and exporter in the next decade.
The field is expected to boost the country's revenue potential because of the higher market prices possible for the high quality, lighter crude found in Shaybah's reserves.

The London-based division of U.S. engineering concern Bechtel won the major upstream part of the Shaybah field work involving the construction of gas-oil separation plants and handling facilities, sources said.

Athens-based Consolidated Contractors International are building infrastructural facilities to develop Shaybah while France's Technip SA is expanding facilities at a processing unit at Abqaiq to handle the crude from the field.
Aramco had awarded a contract to build a 635 km (400 mile) pipeline from Shaybah to Abqaiq and then to export facilities on the Gulf coast to Argentina's Techint.
Shaybah has estimated reserves of around seven billion barrels.
